A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EF-Landing work. All 38 pages in each version, including Appendices A–D, are readable, and corresponding text, equations, tables, and figures can be reliably matched.

before.justification: Section 7 and Appendix D report original distributed PCA experiments on synthetic data and neural-network experiments on MNIST and CIFAR-10, with results in Figures 2–3 and 5–19.

after.justification: Section 7 and Appendix D retain these original PCA and orthogonally constrained VGG16/ResNet-18 experiments and their reported results.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1 and 3 retain the same Euclidean-gradient compression, error feedback, momentum, clipping, and block-wise updates. Changes to convergence-bound indices do not alter the algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic distributed PCA problems and MNIST/CIFAR-10 classification tasks, including the same decentralized and centralized multiple-local-update comparison scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments: Landing, QR retraction, the penalty method, DRSGD and DRGTA in Figures 16–17, and Algorithm 1 of Zhang et al. (2024) in Figures 18–19.

E3.justification: Section 7 and Appendix D retain the same data splits, preprocessing, dimensions, node counts, training schedules, compression settings, and evaluation metrics. Hyperparameter Tables 2–14 are unchanged.

E4.justification: The penalty-strength sensitivity comparisons in Appendix D.3 and Figures 10–15 are unchanged. No ablation, robustness test, error analysis, or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The experimental figures and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All empirical findings and result entries are retained. Experimental plot images in Figures 2–3 and 5–19 are identical, including the accuracy, communication, gradient-norm, and constraint-violation results.

T1.justification: Several bounds now include the initial iterate: lower summation limits change from k = 1 to k = 0 in Corollary 5.12, Theorems 5.14, 5.16 and C.1, and Equations 68–69, 71 and 73. This aligns their averaging ranges with Theorem 5.9 and its telescoping proof. Convergence orders and proof strategies remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about retraction-free communication-efficient optimization, sharp convergence guarantees, asymptotic linear speedup, and extension to block-wise constraints.

C2.justification: The explanations for Euclidean-gradient compression and error feedback, interpretations of experimental advantages, and qualifications concerning compression aggressiveness and one-way communication are unchanged.

D1.justification: The PyTorch and single-GPU implementation statements, synthetic-data generation instructions, preprocessing descriptions, and Appendix D hyperparameters are unchanged. No code or data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 2, the bibliography, and the positioning relative to Landing, error-feedback methods, and distributed manifold optimization are unchanged.

P1.justification: Local notation edits standardize X⋆ and m⋆ to X* and m*, and correct the quantified sample symbol to ξ_i in Assumption 5.1. The arXiv version/date also changes. Paragraphs and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 18–19 receive small caption-spacing corrections after a comma. All embedded figures are identical; axes, legends, table structures, and overall page organization are retained.

improvement.justification: The corrected summation limits align affected bounds with the existing k = 0 through K − 1 analysis in Theorem 5.9 and Equation 61. Together with notation fixes, this modestly improves mathematical consistency and readability. The method, experimental evidence, and main conclusions remain unchanged.
